messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating‑point numbers have a limited mantissa, so each arithmetic operation rounds the exact real result to the nearest representable value. Because the rounding is applied after every addition, the intermediate sum in \((a+b)+c\) can be rounded differently than the intermediate sum in \(a+(b+c)\), leading to distinct final values. Consequently, the finite precision and rounding errors of floating‑point arithmetic break the mathematical associativity of addition.
